item.title: The 1776 North Carolina Constitution — Wed Sep 23, 5:00 PM — Wilson Library
item.description:
North Carolina’s 1776 Constitution grew out of two crises: an east-west power struggle that erupted into the War of the Regulation, and a fight for political representation against an increasingly hostile English government. This lecture traces that story back to the religious and political conflicts of 17th-century Britain, through the migrations and economic pressures that shaped colonial North Carolina, to the document that remains the state’s constitutional foundation today.
The lecture is presented by an interdisciplinary team from Carolina Law, the History Department and the University Libraries.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.description: Many experiments have demonstrated the use of optically active central spin systems, such as color centers in diamond, self-assembled quantum dots, and rare-earth ions, for applications in quantum communications and sensing. If the proximal nuclear spins in these systems are controllable, they can be repurposed from a source of electron spin decoherence to a long-lived memory for quantum information storage. We consider electron-mediated nuclear spin control via optical pulses applied to the central electron spin. This shaggy picaresque follows down-and-out jukebox operator Macabee Cohn (played with deadpan melancholy by David Brisbin) who wanders the borough's cheap tenements, dive bars, and derelict streets in search of a mysterious woman in a striped dress.
Hartman co-owned the NoHo landmark the Great Jones Cafe, often credited with introducing Cajun cooking to downtown NYC, and a magnet for indie film and music communities for decades. He rolled his gumbo money into the production of NO PICNIC and subsequently started the beloved Two Boots Pizzeria on Avenue A to scare up enough money for post-production expenses.

item.title: Applied Thematic Analysis (online) — Fri Sep 25, 10:00 AM
item.description:
It’s Monday morning and you open your qualitative research project folder. Thousands of pages of text, distributed across 90 in-depth interviews, await. What’s next? This workshop provides a roadmap for conducting an applied thematic analysis, through all major steps in the analytic process. Participants will learn the benefits of writing a qualitative data analysis plan, to ensure that the data collected are analyzed in a way that best informs the research question(s) and fulfills the study’s objectives.
The instructors will demonstrate how to inductively identify themes, transform those themes into codes, and aggregate codes into an evidence-based codebook that is easy to use and that will inform the study’s research question(s). Some time will be spent on the topic of integrating codes and interpreting thematic structure. Basic data reduction techniques will also be presented Hands-on exercises are included for those who wish to practice the concepts learned.

UNC Global Affairs is pleased to partner with the Association for Diplomatic Studies and Training (ADST) to host a traveling exhibition on the history of American diplomacy, “United States Diplomacy: From Its Beginnings to Today.”
Created with support from the Una Chapman Cox Foundation, the 21-panel exhibition celebrates diplomatic accomplishments and traces diplomacy’s role across America’s 250-year history, from Benjamin Franklin’s mission to Paris during the Revolutionary War, to 21st-century challenges such as transnational terrorism, climate change and global health.
The exhibition begins during the opening reception for Diplomacy Week 2026 on Monday, Sept. 28, and will be on display in the FedEx Global Education Center until Friday, Oct. 2.

item.description:
This course will be offered over two mornings (9/30/2026 and 10/2/2026 from 10am – 2pm US Eastern) via Zoom only. Attendance is required as the course will not be recorded.

item.title: Mental Health Awareness for Leaders — Wed Sep 30, 12:00 PM
item.description:
Managing individuals who may be struggling with stress, anxiety, depression and other mental health concerns can be a difficult balancing act. Your role is to manage performance and to bring out the best in your workforce, but accomplishing this often requires you to express concern and support when employees struggle emotionally. Managers often feel uncomfortable in this aspect of their role and may lack the important skills of “emotional management.” This course covers ways employees may present their distress and offers insights and strategies on forging supportive empathic alliances within the role of manager. The session also identifies common mistakes managers make in responding to employees in distress and explains communication skills that express support and convey positive expectancy. Participants are also given information on how to refer employees to the Employee Assistance Program.

item.description:
It's time to play the third annual Cyber Bowl, a month-long competition to determine which North Carolina university is the most cyber savvy.

item.title: AI in Research Series – AI and Simple Statistics — Thu Oct 1, 1:00 PM
item.description:
AI in Research: Driving Innovation Forward
Discover how artificial intelligence can streamline workflows, uncover hidden patterns, and empower breakthroughs in your field. Learn practical applications of AI through Odum Institute AIR series that can revolutionize your research process.
AI, for example ChatGPT, may be used to carry out some tasks commonly used by social scientists. Examples include Pearson’s chi-square test, Fisher’s exact test, Student’s t-test, power calculations and non-centrality parameters. The quality of responses has varied to this point and may continue to at the time of the class. Examples will be given.
You must have a UNC Chapel Hill Onyen to register and attend this course. No registration fees required but you must register to secure your spot and receive the Zoom link.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: Mitigating Bias in AI — Thu Oct 1, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Generative AI can reflect human bias through the data it is trained on, the choices made by its developers, and the ways we use it. The good news is that we can take steps to reduce that bias. In this workshop, you’ll learn how to write thoughtful prompts, question AI-generated responses, and guide GenAI tools toward more balanced and reliable results.
This workshop is offered by the University Libraries and will be led by librarian Michele Hayslett.
This workshop is being offered remotely via Zoom only. You can register through the library calendar. Registrants will receive a Zoom link; those on the waitlist will not receive a Zoom link unless they are bumped up to a registered spot.
All registrants however, will receive access to the meeting recording and resources.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: ‘Never A Bad Peace: Celebrating 250 Years of American Diplomacy’ with Adam Howard — Thu Oct 1, 5:30 PM — FedEx Global Education Center
item.description:
In 1783, Benjamin Franklin wrote, “May we never see another War! for in my Opinion there never was a good War, or a bad Peace.”
In this Diplomatic Discussion, the keynote lecture of Diplomacy Week 2026, Adam Howard, former chief historian at the U.S. Department of State, discusses three pivotal moments in American history shaped by the work of talented diplomats: the Revolutionary War, the Civil War and the aftermath of World War II.
Vice Provost for Global Affairs and Chief Global Officer Barbara Stephenson conducts a fireside chat, followed by questions from students in the audience. Afterwards, join Howard and Stephenson in the Florence and James Peacock Atrium for pizza and discussion.
